shared_memory_pools.description: RFC 0008 PR plan PR 4: named cross-agent memory pools with config-based ACL enforcement (RFC 0008 §H, Open Question 13). Deny-by-default — agents not in a pool's `readers` / `writers` lists raise SharedMemoryPermissionError. Sensitive pools (`sensitive: true`) cannot be published into via `MemoryFacade.publish_to_pool` regardless of writer ACL — RFC 0008 §H safety constraint #3.

id.description: Unique agent identifier (lowercase, hyphens allowed). The 'pool-' prefix is reserved for synthetic SharedMemoryPool agent IDs (RFC 0008 §H, PR plan PR 4) — declaring a real agent with this prefix would silently namespace-collide with a hypothetical pool of the same suffix in the shared episodic SQLite store. Validate-time rejection prevents the operator footgun (PR #223 pass-2 review S3-schema).

type.description: Agent type: task (responds to assigned work) or persona (event-driven with autonomy)

instructions.description: Inline system prompt instructions for task agents. Mutually exclusive with 'instructions_file'. Either field is required when type=task.

instructions_file.description: Repo-root-relative path to a markdown file containing system prompt instructions. Must live under prompts/. Mutually exclusive with 'instructions'. The pattern enforces the prompts/ subtree at validate time as defense-in-depth; the runtime loader (agents.prompt_loader) is the authoritative deny-by-default control.

max_llm_calls.description: Maximum number of LLM calls per task (agent-level default for cascade)

max_tokens.description: Maximum output tokens per LLM call (agent-level default for cascade)

allOf.$comment: Conditional validation: each if-block requires 'type' to be present (required: [type]) so that v0.1 agents — which omit the 'type' field entirely — skip these conditionals and pass validation without 'persona' or 'instructions'. This is intentional backward-compatibility: v0.1 and v0.2 agent entries coexist in the same agents.yaml.

then.$comment: Persona agents must not declare task-agent prompt fields. Both 'instructions' and 'instructions_file' are silently ignored by create_persona_agent, which makes them an operator footgun; rejecting at validate time surfaces the misconfiguration before runtime.

allOf.$comment: Task agents must declare exactly one of 'instructions' or 'instructions_file'. 'oneOf' (rather than 'anyOf') catches the both-fields-set conflict at validate time; the runtime loader still enforces the same rule as defense-in-depth.

Safety net: if an agent configures persona-specific fields but omits 'type', require 'type' to prevent silent misconfiguration. Without this, a v0.2 persona agent missing 'type' would skip both conditionals above and validate without 'instructions' or 'persona' being required.

timezone.description: RFC 0021 PR 2: IANA timezone name (e.g. 'UTC', 'America/Los_Angeles', 'Asia/Tokyo') used to render the persona's now-anchor and recency tags. Defaults to 'UTC' when absent. Validated by zoneinfo.ZoneInfo at construction so a typo surfaces at startup rather than at first prompt render.

behavior.description: Structured behavioral dimensions (RFC 0005). Replaces free-text personality.traits / communication_style / decision_making. Individual dimensions are optional — omitted dimensions default to their middle value.

tick_interval_seconds.description: Seconds between autonomous tick cycles. RFC 0024 PR 2 introduces `autonomy.timers` as the per-agent replacement; both knobs are accepted side-by-side through v0.3.3 — `timers` wins when both are present. Phase 5 (v0.4.0) emits a deprecation warning on this field; Phase 6 (v0.5+) removes it.

timers.description: RFC 0024 PR 2: per-agent scheduled wake timers. Each entry registers a periodic `ScheduledWake(timer_id, callback_kind)` producer with the agent's EventLoop. Empty list (`timers: []`) is the v0.3.3 default — stock personas ship with no timers so an idle persona pays nothing. When both `timers` and the legacy `tick_interval_seconds` are present, `timers` wins and the loader emits an INFO log. The `scheduled_wakes` SQLite table (per RFC 0024 §OQ §1) is the persistence target for this list; PR 2 ships the table + cache class, and the startup-rebuild wiring (so a restart mid-jitter-window does not fire immediately) lands in the PR 2.1 follow-up — `agents.yaml` stays canonical regardless.

id.description: Stable identifier for this timer. Unique within the persona. Carried on every `ScheduledWake(timer_id=...)` so dashboards can attribute wakes per timer.

interval_seconds.description: Period in seconds. Floor of 1.0s mirrors `EventLoop._MIN_INTERVAL` and `TickScheduler._MIN_INTERVAL` — per RFC 0024 §Security Considerations, sub-second intervals are a busy-loop class (one LLM call per fire) and are rejected at schema validation; `EventLoop.register_timer` rejects at the API boundary as defense-in-depth.

kind.description: Callback identifier carried on the synthesised `ScheduledWake(callback_kind=...)`. Operator-visible string — chosen examples include `memory_consolidation` (RFC 0027) and `reflection`. Phase 2 ships the mechanism; the policy (which kinds trigger what) is owned by the RFC that introduces the consumer.

jitter_max_seconds.description: Re-arm jitter envelope: each fire's next delay is drawn from `[interval_seconds - jitter_max_seconds, interval_seconds + jitter_max_seconds]`. Spreads fan-out when many identically-configured personas restart together (per RFC 0024 §C). Default 0.0 reproduces the PR 1 no-jitter cadence. `EventLoop.register_timer` enforces `jitter_max_seconds <= interval_seconds - 1.0` (the busy-loop floor) so the lowest possible draw never crosses `_MIN_INTERVAL`; configurations that exceed this slack are rejected at startup.

salience_threshold.description: RFC 0024 PR 3b: minimum write-side salience for the EventLoop's MemoryWriteBus subscriber to enqueue a SalienceWake. Strict `>` — a value at exactly this threshold is suppressed. Default 0.95 is strictly above PR 3a's conservative-scoring maximum (`REFLECTION_CONTRADICTION_SALIENCE = 0.6`), keeping salience wakes off under stock scoring; the inequality is the v0.3.3 'Idle Truly Idle' release-gate invariant, asserted from both sides in `agents.tests.test_event_loop_salience_default_off`. The calibration follow-up flips this default after the v0.3.x sequencing §OQ §3 salience-distribution data sample is collected.

salience_rate_max_per_sec.description: RFC 0024 PR 3b: per-agent rolling-1-second cap on SalienceWake enqueues. DoS guard per RFC 0024 §Security Considerations — a malicious or buggy memory write with `salience: 1.0` on a high-frequency loop must not DoS the agent. Default 10/sec matches the RFC's named value; configurable downward by deployments that want a tighter cap.

max_actions_per_tick.description: Maximum actions executed per tick cycle

idle_after_ticks.description: Reduce activity after this many consecutive idle ticks

memory.description: Memory configuration for persona agents (RFC 0005) and memory-enabled task agents (RFC 0008 PR plan PR 2).

enabled.description: RFC 0008 PR plan PR 2: opt-in flag for task-agent MemoryFacade. Deny-by-default — preserves existing stateless task-agent behaviour. Persona agents ignore this flag (their memory tiers are always initialised by initialize_persona_agents).

min_score.description: RFC 0008 PR plan PR 2: default relevance floor passed to MemoryFacade.retrieve_relevant. PR 2a raises the default from null to 0.20 (matches DEFAULT_EPISODIC_MIN_SCORE) so low-score entries do not cross the system-prompt trust boundary (OWASP LLM01). Set to null to disable filtering — only safe when downstream consumers re-rank or sandbox the entries.

episodic_cap.description: RFC 0008 PR plan PR 2: episodic-tier size cap for the eviction follow-on PR. Stored on the schema now so `memory.enabled: true` configs do not need to migrate when eviction lands.

ttl_low_importance_days.description: RFC 0008 PR plan PR 2: TTL (in days) for entries with importance < 0.3. Honoured by the eviction follow-on PR.

eviction_cadence_seconds.description: RFC 0008 PR plan PR 2: eviction-loop cadence. Honoured by the eviction follow-on PR.

procedural_memory.description: RFC 0008 PR plan PR 5 (Phase 4b): confidence-decay knobs for the procedural tier. Decayed confidence is computed at recall time as `c0 * exp(-lambda_per_day * age_days)`; entries below `c_min` are filtered from `retrieve_procedures` and evicted by the periodic loop. Entries in `[c_min, stale_confidence_alert_threshold)` emit a `stale_memory_injection` structured log on admission so operators can spot procedural drift before it impacts execution.

lambda_per_day.description: Per-day exponential decay rate. The default 0.01 yields a ~69-day half-life; raise for fast-changing domains, lower for stable procedural knowledge. A 30-day post-merge calibration review (RFC 0008 Open Question 12) revisits the default.

c_min.description: Decayed-confidence floor below which procedural entries are excluded from `retrieve_procedures` and evicted by the periodic loop.

stale_confidence_alert_threshold.description: Entries admitted with decayed confidence in `[c_min, stale_confidence_alert_threshold)` emit a `stale_memory_injection` warning log (RFC 0008 Open Question 5). Must be >= `c_min`; the facade rejects inverted pairs at startup.

society.description: RFC 0029 Phase 1: optional society-tier (cross-agent) storage backend for the MemoryStore facade. v0.3.2 ships single-agent mode only — a configured `dsn` is accepted by the schema but ignored by the facade; every society-tier method raises SocietyBackendUnavailable until the Postgres society backend lands in RFC 0029 Phase 3 (v0.4.0). An absent block or `dsn: null` selects single-agent mode.

dsn.description: PostgreSQL DSN for the shared society store (e.g. `postgres://host/db`). `null` (the default) selects single-agent mode: every society-tier MemoryStore call raises SocietyDisabled. Consumed from RFC 0029 Phase 3 onward; accepted-but-ignored in Phase 1.

db_path.description: Path to the shared SQLite memory database

interaction_idle_timeout_sec.description: Idle window (seconds) after which an open multi-turn interaction is closed by IdleGapDetector (RFC 0020 §B). Threaded into InteractionTracker at runtime startup.

enabled.description: Whether the agent can use memory tools (store_note, etc.)

max_notes.description: Per-agent note cap; oldest low-access notes pruned when exceeded

auto_reflect_after.description: Inject reflection nudge after N interactions

inject_recent_notes.description: Number of most relevant notes to include in context per LLM call

retention_days.description: Hard-delete compressed episodes older than this many days (per E7.2)

facts.description: Declarative-fact tier configuration (RFC 0026 §E). The tier injects subject-indexed (subject, predicate, object) tuples — extracted at interaction close per RFC 0026 PR 2 — into the persona's working memory between the relationship and notes tiers. Operators can disable the tier for diagnostic purposes; the per-tier soft slice tunes how much of the RFC 0017 1500-token allocator the facts tier may consume per event.

enabled.description: Whether the persona-runtime injects declarative facts into the working memory ``facts_context`` section. Setting to false skips the FactStore.recall call and admits no facts; the extractor (PR 2) still runs at interaction close so disabling this knob does not prevent fact writes.

budget_tokens.description: Per-tier soft slice of the RFC 0017 1500-token allocator (default ≈13% per RFC 0026 OQ #2). The shared allocator still owns the 1500-token cap; this knob bounds how much of that cap the facts tier may consume on a single event so the notes / episodic tiers downstream still receive their share when many facts apply to the sender.

decay_rate.description: Per-cycle trust decay rate toward neutral (0.5). Higher values cause faster trust erosion without reinforcement.

conversation_window.description: RFC 0034 Phase 1: per-agent override for the conversation-window transcript reconstruction. The persona runtime rebuilds the LLM `messages` array from the channel store each turn so the model sees the in-progress conversation as a transcript (closes ISSUE-0052). All properties are optional; an omitted block (or omitted key) inherits the top-level `conversation_window` defaults from config/optimization.yaml. Wired into the runtime by RFC 0034 Phase 1 PR 3.

enabled.description: Whether the persona runtime reconstructs the conversation window for this agent. false ⇒ the LLM `messages` array is seeded with the current event only (pre-RFC-0034 behaviour) — the operator escape hatch if Phase 3 telemetry surfaces a regression.

max_turns.description: Upper bound on replayed transcript turns. Oldest turns drop first (FIFO) once the count is exceeded (RFC 0034 OQ #2 resolution 2a).

max_tokens.description: Token budget for the replayed transcript, separate from the RFC 0017 system-prompt memory budget. Oldest turns drop first (FIFO) once the budget is exceeded; the tighter of max_turns / max_tokens binds per turn.

shared_memory_pool.description: RFC 0008 PR plan PR 4: ACL + retention settings for one named shared pool. Reader and writer ACLs are deny-by-default.

readers.description: Agent IDs allowed to read from this pool. Deny-by-default — agents not listed raise SharedMemoryPermissionError.

writers.description: Agent IDs allowed to write into this pool. Deny-by-default.

max_entries.description: Maximum entries retained in the pool. FIFO eviction on `created_at` ascending when exceeded — RFC 0008 PR plan PR 4 documents why §G hybrid scoring does not apply to shared pools.

required_confidence.description: Writers must supply `confidence >= required_confidence`; lower values are rejected at write time.

sensitive.description: When true, `MemoryFacade.publish_to_pool` rejects all writes regardless of writer ACL — RFC 0008 §H safety constraint #3.
